headings: Risks Relating to Our Financial Matters
An inability to source capital to supplement our available cash resources and existing credit facilities could cause us to have inadequate liquidity and could materially and adversely affect us.

We and our subsidiaries may be restricted under the terms of our and their indebtedness from paying dividends or distributions under certain circumstances, which could materially and adversely affect our liquidity.

Restrictions in agreements governing us and our subsidiaries' indebtedness may prevent us and our subsidiaries from engaging in certain beneficial transactions, which could materially and adversely affect us.
Our use of derivative instruments, including our IPM agreements, to manage risks could have a significant adverse or otherwise volatile effect on our earnings reported under GAAP and our liquidity.
Our ability to declare and pay dividends and repurchase shares is subject to certain considerations.
Risks Relating to Our Operations and Industry
We may not be able to purchase or receive physical delivery of sufficient natural gas to satisfy our delivery obligations under the SPAs, which could have a material adverse effect on us.
We are subject to significant construction and operating hazards and uninsured risks, one or more of which may create significant liabilities and losses for us.
Changes to U.S. trade policy could have a material adverse effect on our business, contracts, financial condition, operating results, cash flow, liquidity and prospects.
We face competition based upon the international market price for LNG.
Outbreaks of infectious diseases, such as COVID-19, at one or more of our facilities could adversely affect our operations or business.
Risks Relating to Regulations
Our interstate natural gas pipelines and their FERC gas tariffs are subject to FERC regulation. If we fail to comply with such regulation, we could be subject to substantial penalties and fines.

Existing and future safety, environmental and similar laws and governmental regulations could result in increased compliance costs or additional operating costs or construction costs and restrictions.
Pipeline safety and compliance programs and repairs may impose significant costs and liabilities on us.
Additions or changes in tax laws and regulations or variables impacting our tax obligations could potentially affect our financial results or liquidity.
paragraphs: The following are some of the important factors that should be considered when investing in us, as such risk factors could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows or have other adverse impacts, and could cause actual results to differ materially from estimates or expectations contained in our forward-looking statements. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us, or that we currently deem to be immaterial, may also adversely affect our business, contracts, financial condition, operating results, cash flows, liquidity and prospects.

As of December 31, 2025, we had, on a consolidated basis, $1.1 billion of cash and cash equivalents (of which $182 million was held by our consolidated variable interest entities ("VIEs")), $485 million of restricted cash and cash equivalents (of which $22 million was held by our VIEs), a total of $7.2 billion of available commitments under our credit facilities and $23.0 billion of total debt outstanding (before unamortized discount and debt issuance costs). SPL, CQP, CCH and Cheniere operate with independent capital structures as further detailed in Note 10—Debt of our Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements. We incur, and will incur, significant interest expense relating to financing the assets at the Sabine Pass LNG Terminal and the Corpus Christi LNG Terminal, and we anticipate drawing on current committed facilities and/or incurring additional debt to finance the construction of the Corpus Christi Stage 3 Project and the CCL Midscale Trains 8 & 9 Project, as well as the SPL Expansion Project and the CCL Expansion Project if positive FIDs are made on these expansion projects. Our ability to fund our capital expenditures and refinance our indebtedness may depend on our ability to access additional project financing as well as the debt and equity capital markets. A variety of factors beyond our control could impact the availability or cost of capital, including domestic or international economic conditions, increases in key benchmark interest rates and/or credit spreads, the adoption of new or amended banking or capital market laws or regulations, lending institutions' evolving policies on financing businesses linked to fossil fuels and the repricing of market risks and volatility in capital and financial markets. Our financing costs could increase or future borrowings or equity offerings may be unavailable to us or unsuccessful, which could cause us to be unable to pay or refinance our indebtedness or to fund our other liquidity needs. We also may rely on borrowings under our credit facilities to fund our capital expenditures. If any of the lenders in the syndicates backing these facilities was unable to perform on its commitments, we may need to seek replacement lenders or seek alternative financing, which may not be available as needed, or may be available in more limited amounts or on more expensive or otherwise unfavorable terms.

Our ability to generate cash is substantially dependent upon the performance by customers under long-term contracts that we have entered into, and we could be materially and adversely affected if any significant portion of our customers fails to perform its contractual obligations for any reason.

Our future results and liquidity are substantially dependent upon performance by our customers to make payments under long-term contracts. As of December 31, 2025, we had SPAs with initial terms of 10 or more years with approximately 30 different third party customers, with customers under common control being considered a single customer.

paragraphs: Our significant events since January 1, 2025 and through the filing date of this Form 10-K include the following:

•Following our pre-filing in July 2025, in February 2026, we filed an application with the FERC under the NGA for authorization to site, construct and operate in a phased approach the CCL Expansion Project, a potential further expansion of the Corpus Christi LNG Terminal, inclusive of four liquefaction trains and supporting infrastructure, with an expected total peak production capacity of up to 24 mtpa of LNG, inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities.

•In December 2025, we filed an application with the FERC to increase the LNG production capacity of the previously-authorized Corpus Christi Stage 3 Project and CCL Midscale Trains 8 & 9 Project by approximately 5 mtpa, which remains pending at the FERC.

•In March 2025, we received authorization from the FERC under the NGA to site, construct and operate the CCL Midscale Trains 8 & 9 Project, and in June 2025, our Board made a positive FID with respect to the investment in the development, construction and operation of the CCL Midscale Trains 8 & 9 Project and issued a full notice to proceed with construction to Bechtel under a fixed price separated turnkey EPC contract.

•In June 2025, certain subsidiaries of CQP updated the SPL Expansion Project's FERC application, originally filed in February 2024, to reflect a two-phased project, inclusive of three liquefaction trains and supporting infrastructure, maintaining an expected total peak production capacity of up to approximately 20 mtpa of LNG, inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities.

•In August 2025, Cheniere announced the execution of a long-term LNG SPA between Cheniere Marketing and JERA Co., Inc. ("JERA"), under which JERA has agreed to purchase approximately 1 mtpa of LNG from Cheniere Marketing on an FOB basis from 2029 through 2050. The purchase price for LNG under the SPA is indexed to the Henry Hub price, plus a fixed liquefaction fee.

•In May 2025, Cheniere Marketing entered into an IPM agreement with Canadian Natural Resources Limited to purchase 140,000 MMBtu per day of natural gas at a price based on the Japan Korea Marker, less fixed LNG shipping costs and a fixed liquefaction fee, for a term of approximately 15 years commencing in 2030.
•As of February 20, 2026, over 4,610 cumulative LNG cargoes totaling over 315 million tonnes of LNG have been produced, loaded and exported from the Liquefaction Projects.

•In March, August, October and December 2025, substantial completions of Trains 1, 2 3 and 4, respectively, of the Corpus Christi Stage 3 Project were achieved. In February 2026, LNG was produced for the first time from Train 5 of the Corpus Christi Stage 3 Project.
•During the second quarter of 2025, we completed planned large-scale maintenance activities on two Trains at the SPL Project.

paragraphs: 本公司自2025年1月1日起至本Form 10-K申報日之間的重大事件包括以下事項：
•在2025年7月預先申報後，於2026年2月，本公司向FERC提出申請，根據NGA取得授權，分階段進行CCL Expansion Project的建設與營運，該項目為Corpus Christi LNG Terminal的潛在進一步擴張，包含四座液化裝置及相關基礎設施，預期總峯值生產能力達至24 mtpa的LNG，包含預估的瓶頸改善機會。
•在2025年12月，本公司向FERC提出申請，以增加先前已獲授權的Corpus Christi Stage 3 Project及CCL Midscale Trains 8 & 9 Project的LNG生產能力約5 mtpa，該申請目前仍在FERC審查中。
•在2025年3月，本公司取得FERC根據NGA的授權，進行CCL Midscale Trains 8 & 9 Project的建設與營運，並於2025年6月，董事會對投資開發、建設及營運CCL Midscale Trains 8 & 9 Project做出正面的FID，並發出完整啟動建設的通知給Bechtel，根據固定價格分離式總承攬(EPC)合約。
•在2025年6月，CQP的某些子公司更新了SPL Expansion Project的FERC申請，該申請原於2024年2月提出，現已反映為分兩階段進行的項目，包含三座液化裝置及相關基礎設施，維持預期總峯值生產能力達至約20 mtpa的LNG，包含預估的瓶頸改善機會。
•在2025年8月，Cheniere宣佈與Cheniere Marketing及JERA Co., Inc. ("JERA")簽訂長期LNG SPA，根據該SPA，JERA同意自2029年至2050年以FOB方式購買約1 mtpa的LNG。該SPA下的LNG購價以Henry Hub價格為基準，加上固定液化費用。
•在2025年5月，Cheniere Marketing與Canadian Natural Resources Limited簽訂IPM協議，購買每日140,000 MMBtu的天然氣，價格以日本韓國指數為基準，扣除固定LNG運輸費用及固定液化費用，合約期限約為15年，自2030年起開始。
•截至2026年2月20日，已累計生產、裝載並出口超過4,610艘LNG貨櫃，總計超過315百萬公噸的LNG。
•2025年3月、8月、10月及12月，科羅拉多克里斯蒂第三階段專案第1、2、3及4號機組分別達成重大完工。2026年2月，科羅拉多克里斯蒂第三階段專案第5號機組首次生產液化天然氣。
•2025年第二季，我們完成預期的兩座機組大型維護作業於SPL專案。

headings: 與我們財務事項相關的風險
無法取得資金以補足我們現有現金資源及現有信貸融資，可能導致我們流動性不足，並可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
我們與我們的子公司可能因債務條款的限制，在特定情況下無法發放紅利或分紅，這可能對我們的流動性造成重大且不利的影響。
我們與我們的子公司債務協議中的限制條款可能阻止我們與我們的子公司進行某些有利的交易，這可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
我們使用衍生工具，包括我們的IPM協議，來管理風險，可能對我們根據GAAP報告的營收及流動性產生重大不利或波動的影響。
我們宣佈並支付紅利及買回股票的能力受到某些因素的影響。
與我們營運及產業相關的風險
我們可能無法購買或取得足夠的天然氣以履行我們在SPAs下的交付義務，這可能對我們造成重大不利影響。
本公司面臨重大之建設與營運風險及未投保風險，其中之一或數項可能導致本公司產生重大負債與損失。
美國貿易政策之變動可能對本公司之業務、契約、財務狀況、營運成果、現金流、流動性及前景造成重大不利影響。
本公司面臨基於國際市場液化天然氣（LNG）價格之競爭。
本公司之一或多處設施若發生傳染性疾病（如 COVID-19）疫情，可能對本公司之營運或業務造成不利影響。
與法規相關之風險
本公司之跨州天然氣管線及其 FERC 天然氣運價率，受 FERC 規範所管制。若本公司未能遵守相關規範，將可能面臨重大處罰與罰款。
現行及未來之安全、環境及類似法律與政府規範，可能導致本公司產生增加之合規成本或額外營運成本或建設成本及限制。
管線安全與合規計畫及修復工程，可能對本公司產生重大成本與負債。
稅法及規範之增訂或變更，以及影響本公司稅務義務之變數，可能影響本公司之財務結果或流動性。
paragraphs: 投資本公司時應考慮下列重要因素，因這些風險因素可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果或現金流產生不利影響，或造成其他不利影響，並可能導致實際結果與我們財務預測或預期有重大差異。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未為本公司所知，或本公司目前認為不重要，也可能對本公司業務、契約、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流、流動性及前景產生不利影響。

截至2025年12月31日，本公司合併後持有現金及現金等價物共11億美元（其中18,200萬美元由本公司合併變動權益實體（"VIEs"）持有），限制性現金及現金等價物共4.85億美元（其中2,200萬美元由本公司VIEs持有），可用於信用融資的承諾總額為72億美元，總負債為230億美元（扣除未償還折扣及發行費用前的數額）。SPL、CQP、CCH及Cheniere擁有獨立的資本結構，詳情請參見我們合併財務明細表的附註10—負債。本公司因資產融資產生，並將產生重大利息支出，特別是Sabine Pass LNG Terminal及Corpus Christi LNG Terminal的資產。我們預期將使用現有承諾融資設施及/或增加負債以資助Corpus Christi Stage 3 Project及CCL Midscale Trains 8 & 9 Project的建設，以及在這些擴張項目取得正FID後，SPL Expansion Project及CCL Expansion Project的建設。本公司能否支應資本支出及重組負債，可能取決於本公司能否取得額外的專案融資以及債務及權益資本市場。許多因素超出本公司控制範圍，可能影響資金的可得性或成本，包括國內或國際總體經濟狀況、關鍵基準利率或信用利差的上升、新或修正的銀行或資本市場法律或法規、貸款機構對與化石燃料相關企業的融資政策的變化，以及市場風險重新評價及資本與財務市場的波動性。本公司融資成本可能上升，或未來借款或發行權益可能無法取得或失敗，這可能導致本公司無法償還或重組負債，或無法支應其他流動性需求。本公司也可能依賴信用融資設施的借款來支應資本支出。若任何支持這些設施的貸款機構無法履行其承諾，本公司可能需要尋求替代貸款機構或尋求其他融資方式，這可能無法在需要時取得，或可能取得的金額較有限，或條件較昂貴或否則不利。
本公司產生現金的能力很大程度上取決於客戶履行長期契約的表現，若任何重要部分的客戶未能因任何原因履行契約義務，本公司可能遭受重大且不利的影響。
本公司未來的營運結果及流動性很大程度上取決於客戶履行長期契約並支付款項的表現。截至2025年12月31日，本公司與約30家第三方客戶簽訂了初始合約期限為10年或以上的長期買賣協議（SPAs），而受共同控制的客戶則被視為單一客戶。
